description.narrative: Insatsen är ett projektstöd till organisationen ”Women in Informal Employment: Globalizing and Organizing” (WIEGO) för genomförandet av projektet "Feminist rightsbased formalisation of selfemployed women workers in the informal economy". WIEGO är ett globalt nätverk av arbetstagarorganisationer, forskare, akademiker och aktörer verksamma inom internationellt utvecklingssamarbete som samarbetar för att stärka kvinnliga arbetstagares röst och representation genom forskning, arbetstagarutbildning och policypåverkansarbete. WIEGO arbetar främst med nationella arbetarledda organisationer anslutna till globala nätverk, med globala nätverk per se och andra globala fackliga federationer inom multilaterala policyområden. Detta gör det möjligt för WIEGO och samarbetspartners att engagera sig både på nationell nivå genom arbetstagarorganisationer och på globala och regionala plattformar för att förändra normativa standarder, vilka krävs för att få genomslag på nationell nivå och vice versa. Det övergripande målet med insatsen är att bidra till att fackliga organisationer, regeringar och multilaterala institutioner i högre grad utgår ifrån den faktiska situationen för egenföretagande kvinnliga arbetare inom den informella sektorn och säkerställer deras mänskliga rättigheter och förutsättningar för ökad ekonomisk egenmakt när arbete formaliseras. I denna insats finns det specifika landallokeringar till följande länder: Nigeria (9,7 %), Senegal (13,0 %), Colombia (7,3 %), Bangladesh (9,9 %) och Pakistan (11,4 %).

The contribution concerns project support to the organisation Women in Informal Employment: Globalizing and Organizing (WIEGO) for implementing the project "Feminist rights-based formalisation of self-employed women workers in the informal economy". WIEGO is a global network of workers organisations, researchers and academics and development practitioners that collaborate to strengthen women workers voice and representation through research, worker education and policy advocacy. WIEGO primarily works with national worker-led organisations affiliated to these global networks, the global networks themselves and other global trade union federations in multilateral policy spaces. This allows WIEGO and collaborators to engage both at the national level through workers’ organisations and in global and regional spaces such as the International Labour Organisation (ILO), the OECD and the African Union to shift normative standards, which are then used to reinforce national level change. The overall objective of the contribution is that identified women workers’ organisations, governments, and multilateral institutions adopt and operationalize a feminist rights-based formalization framework, informed by successful country-level application and aligned with international obligations, to advance the human rights and labour rights of workers in informal employment. In this contribution there are specific country level allocations to the following countries: Nigeria (9.7%) , Senegal (13.0%), Colombia (7.3%), Bangladesh: (9.9%) and Pakistan (11.4%).

The objective of the contribution is that identified women workers organisations, governments, and multilateral institutions adopt and operationalize a feminist rights-based formalization framework, informed by successful country-level application and aligned with international obligations, to advance the human rights and labour rights of workers in informal employment.
This is expected to be achieved by the below five outcomes that together form a clear multi-level pathway to the overall objective:
Outcome 1 (By Year 3)
Women worker leaders in Nigeria and Senegal and at African level establish and sustain inclusive social dialogue platforms with government representatives. This will be done through their gender-transformative demands on social protection, care, and tax policy reflected in joint position papers and policy discussions. These are key components for advancing feminist rights-based approaches to formalization.
Outcome 2 (By Year 3)
Local authorities in Antioquia and Medellín, together with actors in the cooperative movement, use evidence from women-led social and solidarity economy (SSE) care initiatives to inform policy discussions and strengthen enabling frameworks for care provision, decent work, and formalization for women in informal employment.
Outcome 3 (By Year 3)
Corporate accountability actors and due diligence decision-makers recognise and start applying due diligence beyond tier 1 factories in garment supply chains in Bangladesh and Pakistan, shown through public commitments, pilot projects, and new policies that include homeworkers and strengthen worker-centred due diligence.
Outcomce 4 (By Year 3)
Multilateral agencies including the ILO, UN Women, and the OECD, and collaborators in the international labour, feminist and cooperative movements take on the language and principles of feminist and rights-based formalization processes and policies.
